correctness.rationale: Applies to the corrected complete RESULT.md in repairs/3, not the frozen local-threshold wording. The frozen Finding says the balanced allocation becomes a strict local optimum 'at B=2√2'; this is false if inclusive and directly contradicted by its reduced derivative. At S=B/2=√2, 1−2t(S−t)=2(t−S/2)^2, so the derivative of log failure is positive to the left and negative to the right; arbitrarily small balanced transfers then improve success. The repair explicitly excludes equality and makes the derivative’s antisymmetry precise. Rechecked the repaired claim: internal balancing is strict at positive route totals because route success is ab/(1+a+b+ab) and other-route failure is positive. In the balanced family the log-failure derivative has sign (S−2t)[1−2t(S−t)]; when S>√2 both off-center roots are strict failure maxima and the center is a strict failure minimum. The latter lifts to a strict success maximum on the full simplex because changing route totals reduces the best achievable success locally, and any nonzero within-route imbalance strictly reduces success at unchanged totals. Only the center and concentrated endpoints can win globally. Their success difference (balanced minus concentrated) is S²(2S³+S²−8S−8)/((1+S)²(S+2)^4). The cubic has one positive root by Descartes plus the endpoint signs, and is negative at √2; independent bisection gives B_*≈4.357355625886. The endpoint-only max-path proxy follows from the strict increase of p(v/2)^2 in the route budget v. At B=4 the success values are 4/9 and 7/16 (concentrated and balanced); at B=5 they are 25/49 and 3425/6561. All frozen supporting files were inspected including the exact-arithmetic checker, not executed. It does not test the irrational local boundary; the exact sign identity does. The correction leaves the global claim and the open local/global disagreement interval intact. No correlated-passage or ecological field claim is proved.

value.rationale: The repaired theorem exactly separates a meaningful single-route proxy from the true independent-route event. It identifies where local maximization may wrongly favor diversification before the global switch, and distinguishes a degenerate stationary allocation at the onset from an actual strict local optimum. This is a natural benchmark for objective selection and solver interpretation, not validation of habitat restoration recommendations.
